Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR WOODEN WARDROBES (ADJUSTABLE AND NON-ADJUSTABLE TYPE)

( First Revision )
0. F O R E W O R D
0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 May 1986, after the draft finalized by the Furniture Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1967. In this revision, performance requirements of finish have been included. The revised standard also makes reference to the recent Indian Standards for various types of materials allowed in the standard. 0.3 This standard contains clauses which require the purchaser to supply certain technical information at the time of placing orders. The relevant clauses are 5.3, 7, 8.3 and 10.2 ( see also Appendix A ). 0.4 A scheme of labelling environment friendly products to be known as ECO Mark is being introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO Mark shall be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the Resolution No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for ECO Mark, it shall also carry the Standard Mark of the BIS, besides meeting additional optional environment friendly requirements. 0.5 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in this field in this country. 0.6 This edition 2.2 incorporates Amendment No. 1 (January 1992) and Amendment No. 2 (January 1997). Side bar indicates modification of the text as the result of incorporation of the amendments.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers requirements for materials, sizes, construction and finish of wooden wardrobes with hinged doors. 3

IS : 4126 - 1986 2. TYPES 2.1 Wooden wardrobes shall be of two types as follows: a) Wooden wardrobes, general purposes with surface painted or stained and polished; and b) Wooden wardrobes with decorative veneered and polished surface. 3. MATERIALS 3.1 Wood Particle Board -- Wood particle board required for the manufacture of wooden wardrobes shall conform to IS : 3087-1985* and shall be either the flat-pressed single-layer or flat-pressed 3-layer type. Wood particle board used for wooden wardrobes, required to be finished with suitable baking paints or enamel finishes shall be manufactured with only BWR type of adhesives like phenol formaldehyde. For ECO Mark, the particle board shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 3087 : 1985* for ECO Mark purposes. 3.2 Veneered Particle Board -- Veneered particle board shall conform to IS : 3097-1980. Both interior and exterior grades of veneered particle board can be used where the wardrobes are to be finished with air-drying paints or varnishes. Where suitable baking paints, enamels or varnishes are to be used, only exterior grade veneered particle board shall be used. For ECO Mark, the veneered particle board shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 3097 : 1980 for ECO Mark purposes. 3.2.1 For wooden wardrobes, decorative veneered type, decorative veneered particle board conforming to IS : 3097-1980 and of the specified timber facing shall be used for the doors and sides. Usually decorative timber is specified as figured teak. 3.3 Plywood -- Plywood used shall conform to IS 303 : 1989 `Specification for plywood for general purposes ( third revision ). 3.3.1 For ECO Mark the plywood shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 303 : 1989 for ECO Mark purposes. 3.4 Blockboard -- Blockboard used in the manufacture of wardrobes shall conform to IS : 1659-1979. For ECO Mark, the block board shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 1659 : 1990 `Specification for block boards ( third revision )' for ECO Mark purposes.
*Specification for wood particle boards (medium density) for general purposes ( first revision ). Specification for veneered particle boards ( first revision ). Spcification for blockboards.

4

IS : 4126 - 1986
3.5 Timber -- Any species of timber specified in IS 13622 : 1993 `Indian timbers for furnitures and cabinets -- Classification' shall be used in the manufacture of wardrobes. 3.5.1 For ECO Mark, only species of timber as specified in IS 13622 : 1993 from sources other than natural forests, such as timber from industrial and social forestry plantations, shade trees from tea and coffee estates, etc, shall be used for the manufacture of wardrobes. 3.6 Medium Density Fibre Board (MDF) -- MDF used in the manufacture of components except plinth or pedestal of wardrobes shall conform to IS 12406 : 1988 `Specification for medium density fibre boards for general purposes', shall be of Interior Grade IGSB if air drying finishes are adopted and Exterior Grade EGSB, if oven drying finishes are adopted. For ECO Mark, the medium density fibreboard shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 12406 : 1988 for ECO Mark purposes. 3.7 Adhesive -- Adhesive used for joinery work shall conform to IS : 848-1974*, IS : 851-1978, IS : 852-1969 and IS : 4835-1979�. 3.8 Wooden screws, wooden dowel pins, almirah locks, handles, hinges, latches and other hardware shall conform to the relevant Indian standards, wherever they exist. 3.9 Paint, enamal and varnish shall be in accordance with the schedule given in IS : 2338 (Part 2)-1967||.

4. DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 4.1 The overall dimensions of wardrobes shall be as follows ( see Fig. 1 ) Height 1980 mm Width 990 mm Depth 610 mm
NOTE -- Minimum clearances required for the wardrobes to be put into recesses or openings, where required, shall be as follows: a) For top 20 mm b) For each side 10 mm c) For depth 5 mm

4.2 Tolerances -- The overall dimensions specified in 4.1 shall not vary by more than � 5 mm.
*Specification for synthetic resin adhesives for plywood (phenolic and aminoplastic) ( first revision ). Specification for synthetic resin adhesives for construction work (non-structural) in wood ( first revision ). Specification for animal glue for general wood-working purposes ( first revision ). �Specification for polyvinyl acetate dispersion-based adhesives for wood ( first revision ). ||Code of practice for finishing of wood and wood-based materials : Part 2 Schedules.

IS : 4126 - 1986

FIG. 1 TYPICAL SKETCH OF A WARDROBE 4.3 The wooden wardrobe shall be rectangular at all the measurable surfaces within a tolerance of �8 mm between the two diagonals of the rectangle. 5. FABRICATION 5.1 Components -- It is advised that wooden wardrobes are first made in component forms and assembled from the components as given in 5.1.1 to 5.3.4. 5.1.1 Sides -- The sides shall be made from wood particle board, or veneered particle board, or plywood, or blockboard or MDF as specified in 3 having a thickness of 20 � 1 mm and shall be prepared for joinery and fixtures as required. The width of the side shall correspond to the 6

IS : 4126 - 1986
width of the top. The side shall extend between the extreme surfaces of the top, the bottom and the back. For front, it may extend to full front where doors are to be inside with front bordered construction or be short of the thickness of doors where doors extend to full width. 5.1.2 Backs -- The backs shall be made from wood particle board panels, veneered particle board, plywood panel, or blockboard or MDF panel as specified in 3 and shall be 10 � 1 mm in thickness. It shall be one piece panel prepared for joinery. The width of the back panel shall correspond to the length of the top panel and the length shall extend between the extreme surface of the top and bottom of wardrobe. 5.1.3 Top, bottom and shelves shall be made from wood particle boards, or veneered particle boards, or plywood, or blockboard or MDF as specified in 3 and shall be of thickness 20 mm with a tolerance of � 1 mm. The length of the top and bottom shall cover the width of the wardrobe and adjusted for the joinery and shall cover the depth including the thickness of the door and allowance for joinery work. 5.1.3.1 Shelving -- The shelves of adjustable types of wooden wardrobes shall be prepared for supporting on shelf bracket. The bracket shall be made of metal sheet not less than 1.6 mm thick and shall be so designed and constructed that the shelf is securely supported and adjustment inside the bracket can be affected easily. Shelf-resting strips of metal shall be provided on the four corners of the wooden wardrobes for adjustment of the shelf. 5.1.3.2 Shelves for fixed shelf type of wardrobes shall be two in number, made of material and thickness given in 5.1.3 and shall be fixed at suitable heights, at the bottom by use of wooden strips. For supporting at the sides, the strips of 15 � 10 mm section, shall be screwed on to the sides by suitable wooden screws, three for each strip, and the shelves shall further be screwed with the back of the wooden wardrobes by driving the screw from the back side. The length of the screws shall be 35 mm for the screws fixing the shelf to the back and 25 mm for screws fixing the supporting wooden strips to the sides. 5.1.4 Doors -- The doors shall be made of wood particle board or veneered particle board, or plywood, or blockboard or MDF given in 3 with thickness 20 �1 mm. The doors shall be prepared to fit the size of the wardrobe and any of the following two methods may be used: a) Door fixing recessed with the side, top and bottom front form as border and hinges fixed on inside surface of sides ( see Fig. 2 ) and border. b) Door fixing on the full front with the hinges on the sides of front edge ( see Fig. 3 ).

MEETING STILES

IS : 4126 - 1986
Dimensions of the side and the door shall be adjusted to suit any of the above methods adopted.
NOTE -- Details of various joints and fixtures are given in Fig. 4 to 6.

5.1.4.1 Meeting Stiles -- The doors shall be in 2-leaf construction with rebate cut at the centre meeting. The rebate shall be 20 mm. Where lipping is provided, the depth of the lipping at the place of the rebate shall be not less than 25 mm. The rebate shall be splayed type as shown in Fig. 7. 5.1.5 The edges of the sides, shelves, the bottom and the top of the doors shall be prepared either by internal lipping or external lipping of filling with suitable wood putty or other suitable material to give proper finish and ability to stand wear of the edges and take necessary fixtures. The components shall also be given filler and undercoat paint so as to be ready for final paint and finishing treatment. 5.2 Joinery -- The joinery shall be generally as described in Appendix A of IS : 3845-1966*. The joining of the sides to the top and bottom shall be either by splined mitre joint or interlocked mitre joint or straight mitre joint fixed by screws driven angularly or supported by wood strip, or by butt joint without or with dowels or half-lapped joining. The joints shall be well secured glue and suitable wood screws for tight and strong fit. Wherever applicable, joints shown in IS : 3845-1966* shall be followed for various locations. 5.2.1 The back shall be fixed on to the sides, top and bottom by straight butt joint recessed by half-lap cut and secured by glue and wood screws. Alternatively, it may be fixed by double half-lapped joint or straight butt and secured by glue and wood screws. In the latter case, adjustment shall be made in the width of sides, top and bottom. 5.2.2 For adjustable type of wooden wardrobes, the sides of the wardrobes shall be prepared with bracket holding recesses for adjustment of brackets for shelves. The shelves may be adjustable and shall be securely supported on all the four corners. The brackets shall be so designed and constructed that the shelf is securely supported and that the adjustment of the bracket may be effected easily. Alternatively, metal strips on each corner of the inside of the two sides with holes every 50 mm of height for taking brackets of shelves may be provided. 5.2.2.1 For wooden wardrobes, fixed shelf type, the shelf shall be fixed as in 5.1.3.2. 5.3 Doors -- The doors shall be fixed to the sides internally or externally and by use of either piano hinges or 3-number hinges each
*Code of practice for joints used in wooden furniture.

9

IS : 4126 - 1986
75 mm long and to suit the width of fixing edge by use of suitable wood screws. The wardrobe may be a right door first opening or left door first opening as desired by the purchaser. The door other than the first opening door shall have a latch fixed at the top and bottom to fix it to the top and bottom components. The door shall be provided by suitable almirah locks on the first opening door and suitable lock plate on the other door. The lock shall be internally fixed and the key-hole provided in the door for fixing the key shall have escutcheon plate. The door shall also be provided with suitable almirah door handles. Generally, the wardrobes are with first right door opening arrangements. 5.3.1 The clearance around the door between the sides, top and bottom shall be not more than 1.25 mm. 5.3.2 Hinges -- The hinges shall conform to IS : 1341-1981*, IS : 38181971 and IS : 205-1978. 5.3.3 Hanging Rod -- It shall be of mild steel or aluminium tubular pipe with the wall thickness of not less than 1.60 mm and 20 mm in diameter respectively. This may be nickel or chromium plated conforming to IS : 1068-1968� or anodized in the case of aluminium and fitted to the sides of the wardrobes lengthwise with suitable brackets. The rod may be wooden rod turned to 20 mm diameter. 5.3.4 Pedestals shall be made from solid wood not less than 100 mm high and 65 mm wide and shall be screwed on to the bottom securely by use of suitable screws driven to the bottom of the pedestal in length not less than 50 mm and spaced more than 150 mm.

6. ASSEMBLY 6.1 The various components shall be assembled by means of glue and screws securely fixed under pressure. Before driving the screw, a pilot hole should be driven into the wood panel and the screw should be dipped in glue before driving it in. 7. ADDITIONAL ACCESSORY 7.1 The following additional accessory may be provided, if so desired by the purchaser: Mirror -- The mirror shall be not less than 5 mm thick and shall have suitable dimensions to be fitted into the frame. The mirror shall not be less than 1 200 � 300 mm and 750 � 250 mm in the case
*Specification for steel butt hinges ( fourth revision ). Specification for continuous (piano) hinges ( first revision ). Specification for non-ferrous metals butt hinges ( fourth revision ). �Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on iron and steel ( first revision ). ||Specification for silvered glass mirrors for general purposes ( first revision ).

10

IS : 4126 - 1986
of large and small wardrobes respectively. The mirror shall conform to IS : 3438-1977||. The mirror may be fixed with suitable fixtures with or without beading.

8. FINISH 8.1 Wood Panel Components -- Wood panel components shall be given a coat of primer paint and filler [ see IS : 2338 (Part 1)-1967*]. Wood putty shall be applied to all the surfaces requiring filling and shall conform to the IS : 419-1967. After preparing the surfaces, two coats of enamel paints, that is, an under-coat and a finishing coat, shall be given. The finishing coat shall be synthetic air-drying or a suitable stoving enamel conforming to air-drying or stoving paints for wood work respectively. The enamel or paint shall be of exterior type and of a finish and colour as required. 8.2 The finish shall be smooth, uniformly applied and free from visible defects. It shall be well based and shall not readily chip or flake. The dry film thickness shall not be less than 0.10 mm. 8.3 All other components shall be finished in colour as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 8.4 In case of decorative veneered wardrobes, the decorative veneered surface shall be given a suitable French polish or a suitable wax polish following instructions of supplier of the polish. Clear lacquer based, nitrocellulose or other synthetic finishes may also be used for protective finish. 9. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS OF FINISH 9.1 Every wardrobe shall be checked for good workmanship and shall be free from any stain and warp. 9.2 Resistance of Surface to Dry Heat -- The test sample surface shall be tested for resistance to dry heat in accordance with IS : 5807 (Part 1)-1975. The minimum qualifying average ratings shall conform to 7 of IS : 5807 (Part 1)-1975. 9.3 Resistance of Surface to Wet Heat -- The test sample surface shall be tested for resistance to wet heat in accordance with IS : 5807 (Part 2)-1975�. The minimum qualifying average ratings shall conform to 7 of IS : 5807 (Part 2)-1975�.
*Code of practice for finishing of wood and wood-based materials : Part 1 Operations and workmanship. Specification for putty for use on window frames ( first revision ). Method of test for clear finishes for wooden furniture : Part 1 Resistance to dry heat ( first revision ). �Method of test for clear finishes for wooden furniture : Part 2 Resistance to wet heat ( first revision ).

11

IS : 4126 - 1986
9.4 Resistance of Surface to Marking by Oils and Fats -- The test sample surface shall be tested for resistance to marking by oils and fats in accordance with IS : 5807 (Part 3)-1971*. The test result should conform to 5 and 6 of IS : 5807 (Part 3)-1971*. 9.5 Resistance of Surface to Marking by Liquids -- The test sample surface shall be tested for resistance to marking by liquids in accordance with IS : 5807 (Part 4)-1975. The minimum qualifying average ratings shall conform to 8 of IS : 5807 (Part 4)-1975. 9.6 Resistance of Surface to Mechanical Damage (Type Test) -- The test sample surface shall be tested for impact, cross-cut and scrape tests in accordance with IS : 5807 (Part 6)-1978. The rating shall conform to 5.3 of IS : 5807 (Part 6)-1978.

10 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ECO MARK 10.1 General Requirements 10.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements of quality and performance as specified in the standard. 10.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS environmental consent clearance from the concerned State Pollution Control Board as per the provisions of the Water ( Prevention and Control of Pollution ) Act, 1974 and Air ( Prevention and Control of Pollution ) Act, 1981 alongwith the authorization, if required under the Environment ( Protection ) Act, 1986, while applying for ECO Mark. 10.2 Specific Requirements The product shall conform to the specific requirements given for ECO Mark under relevant clauses of this standard.
NOTE -- The manufacturer shall provide documentary evidence by way of certificate or declaration to this effect to the Bureau of Indian Standards while applying for ECO Mark.

11. PACKING 11.1 All the components parts shall be packed in such a way that no damage is caused to them during transit. 11.2 The purchaser may require the wardrobe to the supplied in knocked down condition, in which case the manufacturer shall prepare
*Methods of test for clear finishes for wooden furniture : Part 3 Resistance to marketing by oils and fats. Method of test for clear finishes for wooden furniture : Part 4 Resistance to marking by liquids. Method of test for clear finishes for wooden furniture : Part 6 Resistance to mechanical damage.

12

IS : 4126 - 1986
the components fully for quick joining and shall supply the purchaser complete details and instructions for fixing.

12. MARKING 12.1 All wooden wardrobes shall be marked with a suitable mark identifying the manufacturer. 12.1.1 The wardrobes may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark.
NOTE -- The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licencc for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers of processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

12.2 The criteria for which the product has been labelled as ECO Mark.

APPENDIX A
( Clause 0.3 ) INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE PURCHASER A-1. The purchaser shall supply the following information to the supplier along with the order: a) Type of lock required, b) Whether locker is required or not, c) Number of adjustable/fixed shelves required, d) Colour of finish, and e) Where alternative methods of construction and finish are specified, they shall be clearly stated in the order.
